chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to us, from Ubaydullah ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Aqaba, from Musa ibn Akeel an-Nimyari, from al-Ala' ibn Sayaba, from Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he said:
Whoever of you dies while holding fast to this matter, waiting (for the reappearance), is like one who is in the camp of al-Qa'im (peace be upon him).

key_terms.الْقَائِمِ: The Rising One, a title for the Twelfth Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for someone who dies waiting for the Imam?
ai.summary: In the context of the Major Occultation (Ghaybat al-Kubra), this hadith from al-Nu'mani reassures the Shia community that spiritual readiness outweighs physical proximity to the Imam. It establishes that those who die in a state of *intizar* (anticipation) share the same merit as those who fought or served in the Imam's actual camp, emphasizing the continuity of the Imamate's authority during his absence.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (15) Ali bin Ahmad narrated from Obaydillah bin Musa from Ahmad bin al-Husayn from Ali bin Aqaba from Musa bin Akeel an-Nimyari from al-Ala’ bin Sayaba that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said: “
Whoever of you dies while still believing in this matter and waiting (for the expected imam) is like one, who will be in the camp of al-Qa’im (as).”
